'''Kostas Antetokounmpo''' ([[Greek language|Greek]]: Κώστας Αντετοκούνμπο) (born May 16, 1998) is a Greek basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] in the United States for the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]].<ref name="realgm">{{cite web|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Kostas-Antetokounmpo/Summary/93018|publisher=[[RealGM]]|accessdate=March 22, 2018}}</ref> He is a {{height|ft=6|in=10}} tall [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]].

==Early years==
Antetokounmpo was born in [[Athens]]. He began playing the sport of basketball with the junior youth teams of [[Filathlitikos BC|Filathlitikos]], in Athens.

==High school career==
After his older brother [[Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis]], was drafted by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], in the [[2013 NBA draft]], Antetokounmpo, along with his parents and his younger brother, Alexis, moved to Milwaukee. He attended [[Dominican High School (Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin)|Dominican High School]], in [[Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin]],<ref name="dominican">{{cite web|last1=Stewart|first1=Mark|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo making a name for himself at Dominican|url=http://archive.jsonline.com/sports/preps/kostas-antetokounmpo-making-a-name-for-himself-at-dominican-b99670083z1-368913091.html/|website=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|accessdate=March 22, 2018|date=February 15, 2016}}</ref> where he played high school basketball, during his junior and senior years. As a senior, he led his team to a state championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://daytonflyers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4218|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo - 2016-17|language=en|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref>

==College career==
After high school, Antetokounmpo moved on to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Dayton]]. In the [[2016–17 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|2016–17 season]], his first with the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Flyers]], he was [[redshirt (college sports)|red-shirted]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2016/10/3/13148932/dayton-flyers-kostas-antetokounmpo-ineligible-redshirt-ncaa|title=Dayton’s Kostas Antetokounmpo ruled ineligible for 2016-17|work=Mid-Major Madness|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref> after being ruled a "partial qualifier",<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2016/10/03/kostas-antetokounmpo-ruled-ineligible-for-dayton/|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo ruled ineligible for Dayton|date=2016-10-03|work=CollegeBasketballTalk|access-date=2018-05-31|language=en-US}}</ref> due to having spent his first two years of high school in Greece.<ref>[https://flyerfaithful.com/kostas-antetokounmpo-may-have-to-sit-the-2016-17-season-out-88140697b419 Kostas Antetokounmpo may have to sit the 2016–17 season out.]</ref> He debuted in the [[2017–18 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|2017–18 season]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kostas-antetokounmpo-1.html|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo College Stats {{!}} College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref> averaging 5.2 points, 2.9 rebounds, 0.4 assists, 0.2 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game, in 15.1 minutes per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/4066490/kostas-antetokounmpo|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref>

On March 22, 2018, Antetokounmpo declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref name="draft">{{cite web|last1=Givony|first1=Jonathan|title=Kostas Antetokounmpo to test NBA draft waters|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22873095/kostas-antetokounmpo-dayton-flyers-enter-nba-draft-test-waters|publisher=[[ESPN]]|accessdate=March 22, 2018|date=March 22, 2018}}</ref> He would later mention that he intends to go pro in the draft that year. On May 4, 2018, Antetokounmpo would be one of a record-high 69 players to enter the [[NBA Draft Combine]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/complete-2018-nba-draft-combine-list-211843026.html|title=Some of college basketball's biggest names highlight NBA draft combine list|access-date=2018-05-31|language=en-US}}</ref> Currently, Antetokounmpo is projected to be a second round selection, similar to his older brother [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo|Thanasis]], due to his lack of notable progress in his freshman season.

==National team career==
Antetokounmpo played with the junior [[Greece men's national under-20 basketball team|Greek Under-20 national team]]. He played at the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship Division B]], where he won a bronze medal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Ndubuisi%20ADETOKUNBO/pid/126901/_//players.html|title=archive.fiba.com: Players|website=archive.fiba.com|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref> During the tournament, he averaged 1.3 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 0.3 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/126901/sid/12474/tid/291/_/2016_FIBA_U20_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html|title=Ndubuisi Antetokounmpo profile, FIBA U20 European Championship 2016 {{!}} FIBA.COM|work=FIBA.COM|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Antetokounmpo was born in [[Athens]], Greece, to [[Nigerians|Nigerian]] parents. He officially became a full Greek citizen in 2016.<ref>[http://www.matrix24.gr/2016/01/vgazi-elliniko-diavatirio-o-kostas-antetokounmpo/ matrix24.gr Βγάζει ελληνικό διαβατήριο ο Κώστας Αντετοκούνμπο {{gr icon}}.]</ref> In addition, along with his younger sibling, Alexis, he has a Nigerian passport, which was granted to him in June 2013, so that he could gain a [[visa policy of the United States|visa]], and be allowed to legally enter into the United States.<ref>[http://www.gazzetta.gr/basketball/article/916698/i-halasmeni-kafetiera gazzetta.gr Η χαλασμένη καφετιέρα  {{gr icon}}.]</ref>

His late father, Charles, was a former Nigerian [[association football|soccer]] player, while his mother, Veronica, was a [[high jumper]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/2013/09/26/226268651/nbas-g-bo-wants-to-bring-hope-to-greece-and-to-milwaukee|title=NBA Rookie Wants To Bring Hope To Greece, And To Milwaukee|work=NPR.org|access-date=2018-05-31|language=en}}</ref> Charles died in September 2017, at age 54.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974785|title=Trail Blazers vs. Bucks - Game Recap - October 21, 2017 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-05-31}}</ref> His oldest brother, Francis, is also a professional soccer player. He is a younger brother of [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player [[Giannis Antetokounmpo|Giannis]], and former NBA player [[Thanasis Antetokounmpo|Thanasis]]. Thanasis currently plays in the [[EuroLeague]]. He is also the older brother of Alexis.<ref name="archdeacon">{{cite web|last1=Archdeacon|first1=Tom|title=Flyers’ Kostas Antetokounmpo tries to live up to his name|url=https://www.mydaytondailynews.com/sports/tom-archdeacon-flyers-kostas-antetokounmpo-tries-live-his-name/meHZJCKf9vQXNYVhHne5gL/|website=[[Dayton Daily News]]|accessdate=March 22, 2018|date=September 23, 2017}}</ref> As a youth, Antetokounmpo was developed by the junior clubs of [[Filathlitikos B.C.|Filathlitikos]], in Greece; the same basketball club that also developed his older brothers, Thanasis and Giannis.
